title: Leo XIV (2025)
hookLine: Robert Prevost, an Augustinian from Chicago who served in Peru, becomes pope and greets the world with peace

lines: FIRST WORDS: PEACE BE WITH YOU ALL.
cards: Peace be with you all. Those were the first words, spoken in Italian, by a new pope at the microphone on the balcony of Saint Peter's. Not about himself, or the vote, or the job.
A cardinal had just announced him: Robert Francis Prevost, who had taken the name Leo. He grew up in Chicago. He spent years as a missionary in Peru.
And he belongs to a religious order named for a bishop of North Africa, Augustine of Hippo.

teach.b: First, those words. Leo said this was the greeting of the risen Christ. He was pointing at a scene in John's Gospel.

On the evening of the first Easter, the disciples are hiding behind shut doors, afraid, and Jesus comes and stands in the middle of them. In the Douay-Rheims his first words are simply: "Peace be to you."
No blame for running away. Peace first. Second, the man.
Robert Prevost joined the Order of Saint Augustine, friars who live in community under Augustine's rule.

He went to Peru as a missionary, later served as bishop of Chiclayo, in the north of the country, and became a Peruvian citizen. On the balcony, after Italian, he switched to Spanish to greet his old diocese by name.

teach.h: FOR THEM A BISHOP, WITH THEM A CHRISTIAN.
teach.b: In that first speech he quoted his order's founder, who once told his congregation, in effect, that for them he was a bishop, but with them he was a Christian.
Augustine's point, as Leo used it: the man in white is first of all one more baptized person in the crowd.

teach.h: A NAME FOR A CHANGING WORLD.

teach.b: Speaking to the cardinals in the days after, Leo explained he chose it partly for Leo the Thirteenth, the pope who wrote about the dignity and rights of workers when factories were remaking the world.
Leo said the Church faces another such revolution now, in artificial intelligence, and wants to speak to it in the same spirit.

how: Catholics pray for the pope by name in the Eucharistic Prayer at Mass, and after an election the new pope's name is added to those prayers in churches around the world.

o: the cardinal who announces a new pope's name
a fourteenth-century pope from North Africa
the new pope, Robert Prevost of Chicago and Peru

p: the diocese he served in Peru

s: Leo's first words from the balcony were about the vote
his first words were peace be with you all, which he called the greeting of the risen Christ.
Leo chose his name partly for Leo XIII
the pope who wrote about workers' rights in an earlier revolution.
Leo spoke only Italian from the balcony
he also switched to Spanish to greet his old diocese in Peru.

games.q: you've just been elected pope, and you have to choose a name. the world is changing fast, the way it did when factories arrived. what do you do?
o: take the name of a pope who spoke to an earlier revolution.
take the name of the pope just before you.
games.why: Prevost chose Leo, partly for Leo XIII, who wrote on workers in the industrial age; he tied it to a new revolution in artificial intelligence.

practice: In the Eucharistic Prayer at Mass, the priest prays for the pope by name, and now that name is Leo: say it once, slowly, and think of what the job asks of one person, to speak for peace, to hold together a Church spread across the world, to get up tomorrow and do it again.
If you pray, pray for him by name, in your own words or in silence; if you don't, hold him in mind the way you would anyone with a heavy job.

wordCard.voice: Leo the Fourteenth. Robert Prevost of Chicago, an Augustinian friar and a missionary bishop in Peru, elected pope, who greeted the world with peace.

orig.note: Greek: peace to you, the risen Jesus's greeting to the disciples in John 20.

carryVoice: Your line: peace be with you all. Peace first, before anything else. That's day nine hundred thirty-nine.

sources.ref: first blessing Urbi et Orbi of Leo XIV; address to the College of Cardinals in the days after the election
